The '''2017–18 La Liga''' season, also known as '''LaLiga [[Banco Santander|Santander]]''' for sponsorship reasons,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.laliga.es/en/news/laliga-and-santander-strike-title-sponsorship-deal|publisher=La Liga|date=21 July 2016|access-date=21 July 2016|title=LaLiga and Santander strike title sponsorship deal|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160725161336/http://www.laliga.es/en/news/laliga-and-santander-strike-title-sponsorship-deal|archive-date=25 July 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> was the 87th since its establishment. The season began on 18 August 2017 and concluded on 20 May 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Calendario LaLiga Santander Temporada 2017/18|url=http://www.laliga.es/calendario-2017-2018|website=laliga.es|access-date=21 July 2017|date=21 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170721224912/http://www.laliga.es/calendario-2017-2018|archive-date=21 July 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> The fixtures were released on 21 July 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=LaLiga Santander 2017 - 2018: Calendario, horarios y resultados|url=https://www.eurosport.es/futbol/la-liga/2020-2021/calendario-la-liga-santander-2021-2022-horarios-de-los-partidos_sto5570241/story.shtml|website=eurosport.com|access-date=20 July 2017|language=es|date=19 July 2017}}</ref>

[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] were the defending champions. [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], under new manager [[Ernesto Valverde]], won the league title on 29 April 2018 with four matches to spare.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/apr/29/deportivo-la-coruna-barcelona-la-liga-match-report|title =Lionel Messi hat-trick gives Barcelona La Liga title after win over Deportivo|date=29 April 2018|work=The Guardian|access-date=1 May 2018}}</ref> It was the second part of a [[Double (association football)|double]]-winning [[2017–18 FC Barcelona season|season for Barcelona]], who also won the [[2018 Copa del Rey final]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/apr/21/sevilla-barcelona-copa-del-rey-match-report|title =Departing Andrés Iniesta the star as Barcelona cruise to Copa del Rey|date=21 April 2018|work=The Guardian|access-date=1 May 2018}}</ref>	

[[Levante UD|Levante]], [[Girona FC|Girona]], and [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] were the newly promoted clubs competing in the season, with Girona entering La Liga for the first time in its history. At the end of the season, [[Málaga CF|Málaga]], [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]], and [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo La Coruña]] were all relegated to the [[Segunda División]].<ref name=malaga/><ref name=palmas/><ref name=deportivo/>

==Summary==
Prior to the season, several teams hired new managers, among them the previous season's runners-up [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], who enlisted the services of [[Ernesto Valverde]] from [[Athletic Bilbao]] after the exit of [[Luis Enrique]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Barcelona: Ernesto Valverde replaces Luis Enrique as manager|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40058078|access-date=20 April 2018|publisher=BBC Sport|date=29 May 2017}}</ref> Meanwhile, [[Valencia CF|Valencia]], who had struggled in the previous campaign, hired [[Marcelino García Toral|Marcelino]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Garcia|first1=Adriana|title=Marcelino to take charge of Valencia ahead of 2017-18 season|url=http://www.espn.co.uk/football/valencia/story/3123983/marcelino-to-take-charge-of-valencia-ahead-of-2017-18-season|access-date=20 April 2018|work=ESPN FC|date=11 May 2017}}</ref>

In the transfer window, Barcelona were involved in the [[List of most expensive association football transfers|new world record transfer]], selling Brazilian forward [[Neymar]] to French club [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] for €222&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Laurens|first1=Julien|title=Neymar: how the record-breaking €222m move to PSG unfolded|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2017/aug/04/neymar-how-record-breaking-move-to-psg-unfolded|access-date=20 April 2018|work=The Guardian|date=4 August 2017}}</ref> They replaced him with young Frenchman [[Ousmane Dembélé]], who signed for an initial €105&nbsp;million fee that could rise to €150&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite news|title=Ousmane Dembele: Barcelona agree £135.5m deal for Dortmund forward|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41044659|access-date=20 April 2018|publisher=BBC Sport|date=25 August 2017}}</ref> Defending champions Real Madrid sold striker [[Álvaro Morata]] to Chelsea for €80&nbsp;million and lost veteran defender [[Pepe (footballer, born 1983)|Pepe]] to Turkey's [[Beşiktaş J.K.|Beşiktaş]] on a free transfer,<ref>{{cite news|title=Morata transferred to Chelsea for 80 million euros|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/90minutes/ct-hoy-morata-transferred-to-chelsea-for-80-million-euros-20170719-story.html|access-date=20 April 2018|work=Chicago Tribune|agency=EFE|date=19 July 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Pepe: Portugal defender joins Besiktas from Real Madrid|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40501854|access-date=20 April 2018|publisher=BBC Sport|date=4 July 2017}}</ref> while its largest fee paid during the window was €24&nbsp;million for young defender [[Théo Hernandez]] from city rivals [[Atlético Madrid]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Butler|first1=Michael|title=Theo Hernández's move to Real clouds gentleman's agreement with Atlético|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2017/jul/11/real-atletico-madrid-theo-hernandez-gentlemans-agreement|access-date=20 April 2018|work=The Guardian|date=11 July 2017}}</ref>

Barcelona first topped the table on 16 September after winning 5–0 in its third match of the season against neighbours [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]],<ref>{{cite news|last1=Emons|first1=Michael|title=Barcelona 5&ndash;0 Espanyol|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41212266|access-date=20 April 2018|publisher=BBC Sport|date=16 September 2017}}</ref> eventually making a run of seven wins from the start of the season that ended with a 1–1 draw at Atlético Madrid.<ref>{{cite news|title=Atlético Madrid 1&ndash;1 Barcelona|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41614112|access-date=20 April 2018|publisher=BBC Sport|date=14 October 2017}}</ref> Valencia improved on its previous campaign and began its new season well, with Marcelino getting the best out of players such as Italian striker [[Simone Zaza]] and on-loan Portuguese winger [[Gonçalo Guedes]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Lowe|first1=Sid|title=Marcelino's starvation treatment steering Valencia out of their lean years|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2017/oct/23/marcelino-valencia-la-liga-spanish-football-sid-lowe|access-date=20 April 2018|work=The Guardian|date=23 October 2017}}</ref> Real Madrid struggled in the first half of the season, with problems including a smaller squad, injuries and the comparatively poorer goalscoring form of [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] relative to recent seasons.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Haugstad|first1=Thore|title=5 reasons why Real Madrid are struggling this season|url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/5-reasons-why-real-madrid-are-struggling-season|access-date=20 April 2018|work=FourFourTwo|date=1 November 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Fisher|first1=Jon|title=Zidane insists struggling Real and Ronaldo are 'not that bad'|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/zidane-insists-struggling-real-and-ronaldo-are-not-that-bad/1cg9rt7h58fes1uc8x7nkn0xse|access-date=20 April 2018|publisher=Goal.com|date=18 January 2018}}</ref>

In January 2018, Barcelona added to its attack by spending €160&nbsp;million on Brazilian [[Philippe Coutinho]] from [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], while the end of a transfer ban allowed Atlético to register [[Diego Costa]] and [[Vitolo (footballer, born 1989)|Vitolo]] for action. Real Madrid manager [[Zinedine Zidane]] made no signings.<ref>{{cite news|title=January transfer window report cards: How did each LaLiga team do?|url=http://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2018/02/01/5a72faa3e2704e6e408b467b.html|access-date=20 April 2018|work=Marca|date=1 February 2018}}</ref> [[Málaga CF|Málaga]] were the first team to be relegated, ending its ten-season stay in La Liga with its descent confirmed after a 0–1 loss against [[Levante UD|Levante]] on 19 April.<ref name=malaga>{{cite news|last1=Mayo|first1=Marc|title=Malaga relegated after late loss at Levante|url=http://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2018/04/19/5ad90bf6ca4741e8338b456e.html|access-date=20 April 2018|work=Marca|date=19 April 2018}}</ref> Three days later, [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]]' relegation was also confirmed after the Canarian team lost 0–4 at home to [[Deportivo Alavés|Alavés]] to end its three-year top flight status.<ref name=palmas>{{cite news|last1=McTear|first1=Euan|title=Las Palmas' relegation is confirmed with Alaves thrashing|url=http://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2018/04/22/5adcdd01468aebe2148b45fa.html|access-date=22 April 2018|work=Marca|date=22 April 2018}}</ref>

On 29 April, Barcelona sealed its 25th league title with a 4–2 win at [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo La Coruña]], with [[Lionel Messi]] scoring a [[hat-trick]]. Barcelona still had four matches to play, and it was the second part of its [[Double (association football)|double]], having earlier won the [[2018 Copa del Rey Final]]. The result also made Deportivo the final of the three relegated teams, sending them back to [[Segunda División]] for the first time in four years.<ref name=deportivo>{{cite news|last1=Abrahams|first1=Timothy|title=Deportivo La Coruna 2&ndash;4 Barcelona|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43928594|access-date=29 April 2018|publisher=BBC Sport|date=29 April 2018}}</ref>

A day later, [[Real Betis]], under new manager [[Quique Setién]], booked its entry to the UEFA Europa League following a 2–1 win over Málaga.<ref>{{cite news|title=Betis qualify for the Europa League with win over Malaga|url=http://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2018/04/30/5ae783dc46163f17368b464f.html|access-date=6 May 2018|work=Marca|date=30 April 2018}}</ref> Betis had a chance of occupying Spain's fourth UEFA Champions League spot after Barcelona, Atlético Madrid and Real Madrid, but that was soon taken by Valencia, which returned to the competition for the first time in three years.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Rodríguez|first1=M. Á|title=Valencia return to the Champions League|url=http://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2018/05/05/5aede4a7e2704e055e8b45de.html|access-date=6 May 2018|work=Marca|date=5 May 2018}}</ref> In its second-last match of the season, [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] drew 2–2 with city rivals Betis to confirm seventh place and qualification for the UEFA Europa League at the expense of [[Getafe CF|Getafe]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Mayo|first1=Marc|title=Honours even in vibrant Gran Derbi|url=http://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2018/05/12/5af7320322601da0638b45ee.html|access-date=13 May 2018|work=Marca|date=12 May 2018}}</ref> Barcelona were on track to complete the first unbeaten La Liga season since the Spanish Civil War (and first in a 38-match season), but surprisingly lost its 37th match 4–5 at Levante, having only conceded 24 goals all season to that point.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Begley|first1=Emlyn|title=Levante 5&ndash;4 Barcelona|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44103357|access-date=13 May 2018|publisher=BBC Sport|date=13 May 2018}}</ref>

==Teams==
===Promotion and relegation (pre-season)===
A total of 20 teams competed in the league: the 17 sides from the [[2016–17 La Liga|2016–17 season]] and the three promoted from the [[2016–17 Segunda División]]. This latter three included the two top teams from the Segunda División and the winners of the [[2017 Segunda División play-offs|play-offs]].

[[Levante UD|Levante]] was the first team from Segunda División to achieve promotion, after a one-year absence from La Liga, on 29 April 2017 after winning 1–0 against [[Real Oviedo|Oviedo]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.laliga.es/noticias/el-levante-regresa-a-laliga-santander|title=El Levante regresa a LaLiga Santander|publisher=La Liga|date=29 April 2017|access-date=29 April 2017}}</ref> [[Girona FC|Girona]] were promoted as the runners-up after drawing 0–0 against [[Real Zaragoza|Zaragoza]] on 4 June 2017; this was its first promotion to the top division.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.laliga.es/noticias/el-girona-hace-historia-y-asciende-a-laliga-santander|title=El Girona hace historia y asciende a LaLiga Santander|publisher=La Liga|date=4 June 2017|access-date=4 June 2017}}</ref> It became the 62nd team to participate in the Spanish top level league. [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] was the last to be promoted after defeating [[SD Huesca|Huesca]] and [[CD Tenerife|Tenerife]] in the play-offs, one year after its relegation.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.laliga.es/noticias/el-getafe-regresa-a-laliga-santander|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170628150217/http://www.laliga.es/noticias/el-getafe-regresa-a-laliga-santander|url-status=dead|archive-date=28 June 2017|title=El Getafe regresa a LaLiga Santander|publisher=La Liga|date=24 June 2017|access-date=24 June 2017}}</ref>

The three promoted clubs replaced [[Sporting de Gijón|Sporting Gijón]], [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]] and [[Granada CF|Granada]], which were relegated at the end of the previous season, ending their top flight spells of two, one and six years respectively.

[[Atlético Madrid]] played for the first season at their new stadium, [[Metropolitano Stadium|Wanda Metropolitano]], replacing the [[Vicente Calderón Stadium]], where they played since its opening in 1966.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Lowe|first1=Sid|title=A stadium called Wanda: opening night at Atlético Madrid's new home|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2017/sep/18/a-stadium-called-wanda-opening-night-at-atletico-madrids-new-home|access-date=29 April 2018|work=The Guardian|date=18 September 2017}}</ref>

[[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo La Coruña]] signed a sponsorship contract with [[Abanca]] for renaming their stadium as [[Estadio Riazor|Abanca-Riazor]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rcdeportivo.es/noticia/abanca-y-el-depor-llegan-a-un-acuerdo-de-refinanciacion-de-la-deuda-y-patrocinio-del-estadio|publisher=Deportivo de La Coruña|language=es|date=29 June 2017|access-date=29 June 2017|title=ABANCA y el Dépor llegan a un acuerdo de refinanciación de la deuda y patrocinio del estadio}}</ref>

[[Real Betis]] completed their stadium renovation and it was grown to 60,720 seats, becoming the fourth biggest stadium in Spain.<ref name="RBB"/> Meanwhile, after their first promotion ever to La Liga, [[Girona FC|Girona]] expanded [[Estadi Montilivi]] temporarily for hosting 13,450 spectators.<ref name="Montilivi">{{cite web|publisher=Girona FC|language=ca|access-date=28 December 2017|url=http://www.gironafc.cat/club/entitat|title=Entitat {{!}} Girona}}</ref>

===Zamora Trophy===
The [[Ricardo Zamora Trophy]] was awarded by newspaper ''[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]'' to the goalkeeper with the lowest ratio of goals conceded to matches played. A goalkeeper had to play at least 28 matches of 60 or more minutes to be eligible for the trophy.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/deporte/futbol/primera-division/zamora.html|title=Trofeo Zamora La Liga Santander|work=Marca|date=21 February 2023 }}</ref>
